newsitem.title: PERU: Peru constitutional court head resigns in protest.
newsitem.headline: Peru constitutional court head resigns in protest.

text.p: The head of Peru's highest constitutional court resigned on Friday in protest at the dismissal by Congress of three of the court's members who were opposing a third election bid by President Alberto Fujimori.
"This court was the last hope and bastion of legality and respect for the constitutional law," said Ricardo Nugent at a news conference to announce he was stepping down.

Nugent's resignation, which had been widely expected, left the seven-member Constitutional Tribunal, which has judicial autonomy on constitutional matters, with only three sitting judges when four are needed for a quorum.
On Thursday, the government-dominated Congress dismissed three of the judges who had rejected a law that would have cleared the way for Fujimori to stand again for president in 2000.
"Congress did not take a legal decision but a political one," Nugent said, adding: "I am convinced there is more behind this."
Congress was due in coming days to investigate Nugent's role in the court's rulings on the reelection law, and may have voted to dismiss him as well.
Its vote on Thursday sparked a wave of protest from opposition parties, local media and the Peruvian public.
